questions.prompt: Why are coal and petroleum called NON-RENEWABLE?
options: They are found only in India
They took millions of years to form and can't be replaced in a human lifetime
questions.explain: Fossil fuels form far too slowly to replace what we use.

questions.prompt: Order these crude oil fractions from the TOP of the column (coolest) to the BOTTOM (hottest).
questions.explain: Low boiling point fractions rise to the top; high boiling point fractions stay near the bottom.

questions.prompt: Match each petroleum product to its use.
questions.explain: Each fraction has uses that suit its properties.

questions.prompt: Which fuel has the HIGHEST calorific value?
questions.explain: Hydrogen ≈ 150 kJ/g, far more than LPG (≈ 55 kJ/g).

questions.prompt: Burning 3 kg of a fuel released 180,000 kJ of heat. What is its calorific value in kJ/kg?
questions.hint: Calorific value = heat released ÷ mass burned.

questions.prompt: Which are characteristics of a GOOD fuel? Choose all that apply.
questions.explain: A good fuel gives lots of energy, is easy to handle and affordable, and produces little ash, smoke or harmful gas.

questions.prompt: Why did switching Delhi's buses and autos to CNG improve the city's air?
options: CNG does not produce any carbon dioxide
CNG burns more completely, producing much less soot and smoke than diesel

feedback.0: CNG still produces carbon dioxide. It is cleaner, but not zero-carbon.

questions.explain: CNG (mostly methane) burns cleanly with far fewer soot particles.

questions.prompt: Match each gas released by burning fossil fuels to the problem it mainly causes.
questions.explain: CO₂ is a greenhouse gas; sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides form acids in rain and contribute to smog.

questions.text: Crude oil is separated into useful fractions by fractional ___ at a ___.
questions.explain: Fractional distillation at an oil refinery.

questions.prompt: Give ONE benefit and ONE problem of India using coal to generate most of its electricity.
questions.modelAnswer: Benefit: India has large coal reserves, so coal gives a cheap and reliable supply of electricity for homes and industry, and creates jobs. Problem: burning coal releases carbon dioxide (global warming) and smoke and sulfur dioxide (air pollution and health problems), and coal will eventually run out.
rubric: I gave a clear benefit (cheap, reliable, available, jobs)
I gave a clear problem (CO₂/climate, air pollution, non-renewable)
I explained the impact on people or the environment
questions.explain: Criterion D: weigh benefits against costs.
